question: Does the March 2015 NSCR EPRMP provide independently usable fish data for Guiguinto and Meycauyan Rivers, and can its nekton list be assigned to either river separately?
citation: Department of Transportation and Communications. (2015). Environmental Performance Report and Management Plan (EPRMP) for the North South Commuter Rail (NSCR) Project, Volume I: Main Report, Draft, March 2015.

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Opened the official JICA-hosted PDF through browser text extraction. The PDF page screenshot request timed out; no local copy or page image was retained.
sourceLocators: Cover: printed report marked DRAFT, dated March 2015, and issued under DOTC.
Section 2.3 Freshwater Ecology and Table 2.15: printed pages 96-97; browser-extracted lines 5306-5324.

tableLayoutCheck.textExtraction: The extracted Table 2.15 includes Guiguinto and Meycauyan rows and represents the nekton list as a cell shared across the rows.
tableLayoutCheck.visualPageCheck: Not completed; the browser screenshot request timed out.
tableLayoutCheck.decision: Do not assign any of the four source labels to either river separately.

sourceAccess.reuseTerms: No item-specific open-data license or permission for table reproduction was verified.

sourceScope.sectionContext: The EPRMP describes biological components observed in Guiguinto and Meycauyan Rivers. It says river sediment samples were collected to identify biological populations, comments that fish populations observed in the rivers tolerate pollution, and attributes Table 2.15 to the JICA Study Team.
waterbodyNamesAsPrinted: Meycauyan River (table spelling; prose elsewhere in the report spells Meycauayan)
sourceScope.taxonomicResolution: The table supplies common names only. It does not give scientific names, specimen identifiers, or a taxon-to-river/station crosswalk.

evidenceDecision.decision: Retain the four labels verbatim as historical, shared Guiguinto-Meycauyan retrieval leads. Do not turn the report date into a fish collection date, normalize common names to binomials, or assign a label to one river.

nonClaims: The EPRMP does not verify four scientific fish species; it prints four common-name categories.
The report does not establish which label was found in Guiguinto versus Meycauyan, or at a named station.
The March 2015 cover date does not establish a 2015 fish collection event.
The draft project report is not a complete fish inventory, and its description does not establish current presence, abundance, catchability, fishing access, legal harvest, or consumption safety.
No site geometry, species occurrence, public app row, or publication license is established by this review.
nextActions: Seek a visually inspectable copy of Table 2.15 and any underlying JICA Study Team biological survey notes only if a site-specific or taxonomic crosswalk is needed.
Keep the four common-name labels research-only until scientific identities, fish-specific methods, dates, and river/station attribution are supported by a primary source.
Continue Central Luzon freshwater source review; this merged table does not close Bulacan river coverage or the regional baseline.
